newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Duisenberg calls for automatic sanctions in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg calls for automatic sanctions in EMU.

text.p: The future head of the European Monetary Institute (EMI) Wim Duisenberg said on Wednesday that EU countries running excessive budget deficits should be automatically fined but he doubted whether this will happen.

Speaking at the European Parliament, Duisenberg welcomed the European Commission's proposal for a stability pact for countrees in the third stage of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999 -- when the single currency is created.
The Dutch central bank governor, who is to take over as the EMI head in July 1997, thought the pact plan would have to be strengthened.

"I think in further developing the Commission proposal there will have to be...santions and a degree of automaticity in applying the sanctions," Duisenberg told a meeting of EP's economic and monetary affairs committee.
"There will have to be agreement about that (sanctions) and I do not think there will be very much automaticity," he said.

The Commission proposed earlier this month that EU countries running a deficit in excess of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) after the single currency has been launched be fined a maximum of 0.5 percent of GDP.

But it shied away from proposing automatic sanctions. The decision would have to be taken by EU finance ministers, which opens the way for much wrangling, and there would also be circumstances, such as negative real growth, where the fines could be waved. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
